newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen stabilising on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen stabilising on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares eased for the third consecutive session on Friday and analysts expected them to stay flat on Monday, extending their stabilisation phase after having gained 38 percent since mid-December.

The main market's WIG index fell 70.4 points, or 0.4 percent, to 18,136.2, and turnover fell 19 percent to 203.3 million zlotys ($67.7 million) on all three markets as 48 issues rose, 27 fell and 14 were flat.
"I expect a kind of stalemate session on Monday and significant movement only when investors calm down (after the recent surge)," said Cezary Markiewicz, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Some analysts said a more significant profit-taking correction could hit the market next week, though others expected the bourse to set more 35-month highs before falling.
Some analysts said the potential deeper correction could last about a month and bring the market down to about 16,000 or 15,000 points.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 13.1 million zlotys ($4.4 million) with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,842 points, one percent lower than at the regular session.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 3.8 percent in a 35.9-million-zloty ($11.9 million) turnover at the regular session and rose 0.9 percent in 28.2-million-zloty ($9.3 million) continuous trade.
